comment: feat(libstylist): override sheets — an app restyles a design-system component everywhere with plain CSS: `@stylist override <Component | sheet-id> from "<package>" [within <AppComponent>];` then `.root` (the component's identity, `:is(tag,[tag])`, custom tag and marker alike) and its part names as classes, compiled by `stylistOverride()` (after postcss-nesting) into the overrides layer with a class's specificity; `collectOverrideSheet` (pass 1) and `resolveOverrides` (`/registry`: the package's prefix and namespace, the target sheet, parts and resets, `within` against the app registry, one sheet per design-system sheet) report `invalid-override`, `unresolved-package`, `unknown-target`, `unknown-part`, `unknown-within`, `duplicate-override`, `shared-reset`, `reset-within` and `keyframes-clash` with did-you-mean; `@stylist reset [<part> …];` strips the design system's own declarations of those parts from its stylesheets at build time (`resetCss`/`stylistReset()`: per rule subject, custom properties kept, selector lists split, `:is()` alternatives guarded with a zero-specificity `:where(:not())`, idempotent) with a report of what each reset drops and the layout declarations the override doesn't re-declare (`resetReports`, `formatResetReports`, `[empty-reset]`); the lock takes optional `overrides`/`resets` sections (`toLock(registry, overrideLock)`, `diffLock` kinds `override`/`reset`); `/workspace` adds `compileOverride`, `overridesLayerProblem` and `renderOverridesModule`; `@stylist override`/`reset` in a package sheet are errors; the workspace tooling applies them: `css.overrides` in libstylist.config.mjs (`dir`, `registries` — the design system's css packages, found installed —, `layer`, placed after `components` and before the namespace layers by the loader and the default order statement), override sheets never a package's sheets (an overrides directory inside a sheet directory is left out of its registry and part maps; `compileSheet` refuses them), `buildWorkspace` resolving them against the installed design systems (`collectOverrides`, `from` resolved to the component package installed where the sheet is; `design-system` and `overrides-index` errors), `libstylist build [--check|--watch]` compiling them, writing the generated overrides module and the lock's override sections, printing the reset report (a stale lock lists the entries that moved), `stylistWorkspace()` compiling override sheets into the overrides layer and stripping every stylesheet of the design system's css package of the resets as the app imports it (HMR: a changed reset set reloads the design-system stylesheets, a rebuilt design system the override sheets reading it; the report in the terminal, errors on the overlay; `vite build` fails on `[empty-reset]`, `[unbundled-reset]`, `[overrides-not-imported]` and a stale overrides module; `overrides: false` opts a build out), `libstylist check` rule S310, and the stylelint preset reading override sheets (`directive-syntax`: the override grammar and placement; `sheet-root`: `.root` is the identity, document context before it); override hardening: a reset part styled only through shared `:is()` rules is reset by its guards and counted (no false `[empty-reset]`/`[unbundled-reset]`; `touchedTargets` replaces `droppedTargets`), a guarded rule keeps its custom properties for the reset element, a statement a strip leaves last is ended with `;` (a bundler's concatenation no longer swallows the next stylesheet), layout notes cover zero minima, relative sizes and auto margins and are acknowledged only by a re-declaration under the same conditions (`acknowledgedDeclarations`/`acknowledges` replace `acknowledgedProperties`), an override rule's subject must be `.root`, a part or inside one (`:has()`, `+`, `~` no longer escape the component), `:component()` of the same design system is allowed as context (resolved, locked; `[unresolved-ref]`), a sheet id must be kebab-case (`[invalid-override]` at resolution), `@stylist override Tooltip` points at the `tooltip` sheet, a declaration a design-system `!important` beats is an `[important]` warning (`importantDeclarations`, `importantConflicts`, `designSystemImportants`, `importantWarnings`), `vite build` fails on `[layer-order]` (`declaredLayerOrder`, `bundleLayerProblem`), `vite build --watch` re-reads override sheets and re-transforms them and the design system's stylesheets on every rebuild, and dev HMR looks modules up by posix path
